sentences.text: When a pushing vessel and a vessel pushed ahead are rigidly connected in a composite unit, they are regarded as one power-driven vessel and show the lights of Rule twenty-three.
Otherwise, a power-driven vessel pushing ahead or towing alongside shows two masthead lights in a vertical line and sidelights.
Under International rules, she also shows a sternlight.
Under Inland rules, she shows two yellow towing lights in a vertical line instead of the sternlight.
So from astern at night, a single white light suggests International rules, and two yellow lights mean an Inland pushing or alongside tow.
Inland, on the Western Rivers and other specified waters, a vessel pushing ahead or towing alongside shows sidelights and two towing lights, without masthead lights.
